segments: The tenth dynasty.
The Arab kings.
India, China, and Persia.
And when they reached the land of Bahrain, they were stranded in the deep of the sea (of the water),
because they did not know the entrances.
And the people of Bahrain came out against them in boats,
and they drowned all the Basrans.
And at that time, al-Ma'mun imprisoned four Qurayshite leaders,
who were plotting rebellion against him.
And they made a secret pact with some people to throw fire into the market of the fortress,
and when the king came out to extinguish the fire, they would kill him.
And when al-Ma'mun perceived the plot,
he sent and had the Qurayshites killed at night,
and in the morning he hanged their corpses on trees.
And he also seized Ibrahim, his uncle;
and when he saw that he had grown old,
he spared his life.
This man had learned the art of cithara-playing,
and he used to buy young boys and girls, and sell them, and make a living.
And at that time, two rebels, Sari and Jawri, also seized Egypt,
and they gathered gold like stones.
And when they died,
their sons succeeded them: Ubayd son of Sari over Fustat and the southern side,
and Ahmad son of Jawri over the northern district.
And in the year one thousand one hundred and thirty-seven [826 AD],
Ibn Tahir reached al-Arish;
and Ahmad went out to him and received an assurance of safety regarding the property of his father Jawri—who, when he was dying, said:
"I am ashamed before the earth, for how much gold I am committing to it!" But Ubayd resisted,
because the number of his troops was eighty thousand.
Then in Nisan, Ibn Tahir encamped against Fustat,
and blocked the roads providing provisions by sea and by land.
Then Ubayd sought an assurance of safety for his life and his property,
and he went out to Ibn Tahir,
and they made peace,
and ate and drank.
And in the year one thousand one hundred and thirty-eight [827 AD],
Ibn Tahir encamped against Alexandria,
because the people of Andalusia had seized it,
and had expelled the Christians and Jews, and settled in their houses.
And after nine months of pressing
them, Ibn Tahir {OCR?}, with war and famine,
he subdued them.
And he sent fifty (and five) of them, their families, to Callinicus,
and the rest went to their country.
And he also subdued Africa,
and appointed over them two chiefs from among the upright men who were among them.
And in the year one thousand one hundred and forty [829 AD]
(1140 of the Greeks,
829 of our Lord), Michael, king of the Romans, died,
and Theophilus his son reigned.
